solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guys who aren't rigid agree — that's how more gets added

parts.note: guys are MEN, and men who are not rigid are SUPPLE MEN
to tally is to agree or correspond, as accounts do

explanation.surface: A flexible group of men reach agreement, apparently explaining how extra material gets tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something added supplementally comes as an extra on top of the main part, which is how more is added.

clue.text: Thus top politician conceals his deceptive argument

parts.note: so means thus, in that way

indicators.note: the Prime Minister's letters hold the word his hidden between them

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for Prime Minister, the top politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister hides behind a slippery line of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophism is a clever but fallacious argument, used to mislead rather than persuade honestly.

clue.text: It provides an opening to get a point in the lead

definitions.text: It provides an opening to get a point in the lead

parts.words: It provides an opening to get a point in the lead
parts.note: the device has a hole into which a pencil goes so that its lead (graphite, said 'led') gets a sharp point

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' wants to be read as 'leed', a front position, as if someone gets an opening to score and go ahead; read it as the graphite in a pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: This small desk tool has a hole for the pencil and a blade that shaves the wood to a fine tip.

clue.text: Encouragement to see moderate view

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning behold, urging someone to see
OK can mean moderate, passable, all right

explanation.surface: A prompt to take in a reasonable vista.
explanation.definitionFit: A look is a glance or an appearance; to take a look is to have a view of something.

clue.text: Jumble sale held by the writer's pathetic

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the writer's word, which holds them

parts.note: my is what the writer would say of something belonging to them

indicators.note: to jumble is to mix up, so the letters of sale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that their own jumble sale was a poor show.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface a jumble sale is a British sale of donated second-hand goods; here 'Jumble' is an instruction, not part of the sale's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means paltry or contemptibly small, much like pathetic in its sense of feeble.

clue.text: For instance, accepted by a lot of people? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the nation takes the abbreviation into itself, accepting it

parts.note: a nation is a large body of people
e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an example is widely accepted, and is told the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A negation is a denial or contradiction, the opposite of what was put forward.

clue.text: Fare at higher level to begin with? That's legitimate

indicators.note: says the word for a higher level comes first, ahead of the food

parts.note: above means at a higher level
board is food or meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A query about better food upstairs, answered by calling it all legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means open and honest, with nothing concealed, so legitimate.

clue.text: Sudden problem at work, something a conductor can deal with

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a walkout called without notice by workers

definitions.text: something a conductor can deal with
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a bolt from the sky, which a lightning conductor on a building carries safely to earth

explanation.walkthrough: The conductor looks like a bus or orchestra conductor sorting out a dispute; it is the metal rod on a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both an unannounced industrial stoppage and an electrical discharge from a storm hitting the ground.

clue.text: Robber taking part in two instalments

indicators.note: the piece comes in two separate portions with the other word between them

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
and can mean plus or taking in addition, as in two and two

explanation.surface: A thief collects his share of the loot in two payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' stands for and in the sense of plus; the part is not paid out but split in two around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed outlaw who robs travellers, so a robber.

clue.text: Woman given box containing one or two of Pa's letters

indicators.note: the two letters of Pa hold the and/or phrase between them

parts.note: the two letters spelling Pa, short for father
one or two of a pair means either one, or both together: the logical and/or

explanation.surface: A woman receives a box holding part of a letter from her father.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as P AND/OR A: one of Pa's letters, or two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora was the first woman, given a jar or box she was told never to open.

clue.text: South-eastern state in Europe or America

definitions.text: South-eastern state in Europe or America

parts.words: South-eastern state in Europe or America
parts.note: the same name belongs to a country in the Caucasus at Europe's south-eastern edge and to a US state in the south-east

explanation.walkthrough: Barely cryptic: the trick is only that one name serves both a nation and an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a Caucasus republic on the Black Sea and also the US state whose capital is Atlanta.

clue.text: Flower-girl's language, dropping 'h'

indicators.note: the named letter falls out of the language's name

parts.note: Irish, the Gaelic language of Ireland, read as the language of an Irish girl
taken as written, the letter H

explanation.surface: A flower-girl talks with dropped aitches, like a Cockney flower seller.
explanation.walkthrough: IRIS is also a girl's name, which is why the clue mentions a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, named after the Greek rainbow goddess.

clue.text: Little read novel subjected to abuse

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rarely read novel is treated harshly, perhaps by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book that few read; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-treated has been handled cruelly or harmed, the same as being abused.

clue.text: Conventional armaments I deployed unconventionally

indicators.note: spread out in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits using standard weapons in an odd fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream describes the accepted, ordinary current of opinion or taste, so conventional.

clue.text: Lose after opening of malt whisky

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Islay is a Scottish island famous for its peaty single malts, used for its whisky

explanation.surface: Someone misplaces something after cracking open a bottle of malt.
explanation.walkthrough: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides whose name stands for its smoky malt whiskies.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it down and forget where, so to lose it.

clue.text: Settler on island breaking horse

indicators.note: the inner letters split the horse's name apart

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A settler on an island tames a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like breaking in a horse; here ON and IS break into COLT.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is someone who settles in a colony, a new territory claimed by another country.

clue.text: Versatile worker, in reality, joining old corporation

parts.note: a fact is something real, so in reality means in fact
corporation is a jocular word for a large belly, and tum is the belly

explanation.surface: A handyman really does join an old company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is old British slang for a pot belly, hence TUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is an employee who does all kinds of jobs, a jack of all trades.

clue.text: Second male outside hospital spotted — powerful feller

indicators.note: the biblical name surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: in Genesis Cain, son of Adam, was the second man
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
saw means spotted, noticed

explanation.surface: A second man is seen outside a hospital, perhaps a strong suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like a fellow; it means something that fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a motorised saw used to cut down trees, so it is a powerful tool for felling.

clue.text: Junior minister's position in club oddly suggestive

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first and third

parts.note: racy means slightly risqué or suggestive

explanation.surface: A junior government minister holds a slightly saucy role in a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a clergyman, not a politician: a curate assists the parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the office of a curate, an assistant cleric below the vicar or rector.

clue.text: Just after beginning of false alarm

indicators.note: puts the word for just behind the first letter
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: right means just, fair

explanation.surface: A fake warning has only just gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden scare, and alarm is the sense of fear or shock.

clue.text: Lock aggressive American up inside for hunting female

indicators.note: the reversed soldier goes inside the lock of hair

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, a fighting man

explanation.surface: Lock up a violent American inside, for chasing a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigress is the female of the tiger, a big cat that stalks prey.

clue.text: Open land as alternative to garden

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unfenced land open to the public, like a village green
second meaning: from the phrase ... or garden, meaning ordinary, where it stands as the other choice

explanation.walkthrough: 'common or garden' is a British idiom for ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: A common is shared public grassland, and common is paired with garden in the stock phrase for everyday.

clue.text: Beliefs about someone somehow making a point? True

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a point is made, and confirms it is true.
explanation.definitionFit: A reputation is the general opinion people hold about a person's character.

clue.text: Person seeking quick profit — one without a partner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stock market speculator who buys new shares to sell at once at a profit
second meaning: a man who goes to a party alone

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are slightly specialist: stock exchange slang and the idiom going stag.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag in the City applies for new issues to sell them quickly, and a lone man at a dance is said to go stag.

clue.text: Divine female leads a double life

indicators.note: a double life here means the word for life written twice in a row

parts.note: to be or exist is to have life, so life is the verb form meaning exists

explanation.surface: A goddess runs two separate existences.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the great Egyptian goddess, wife of Osiris and mother of Horus.

clue.text: Agreement with clubs working? Sure thing

parts.note: C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs
on means functioning, switched on
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A deal involving card clubs looks guaranteed to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting together in agreement, so concert is accord.

clue.text: Great service I have reduced

parts.note: Mass is a church service
I have shortened to the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone has cut back on a large church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means huge, so great in the sense of large.

clue.text: Party choices — Newcastle Brown for a couple

definitions.meaning: first meaning: leaders a winning party puts in charge of government
second meaning: two examples, the Duke of Newcastle and Gordon Brown, both premiers

explanation.walkthrough: Newcastle Brown is a British beer and party suggests drinks; but Newcastle and Brown are two separate holders of the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of British governments, chosen by their parties, include the 18th-century Duke of Newcastle and Gordon Brown.
